cards.front: Recall a key point about Television
cards.back: Television is one of the most influential media forms, combining visual, audio, and written codes to tell stories and communicate ideas to mass and niche audiences.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Television
cards.back: Traditional broadcast TV used scheduling to target audiences — primetime (7-10pm) for mass audiences, late night for niche content, daytime for specific demographics.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Television
cards.back: Streaming services (Netflix, Amazon Prime, Disney+) have disrupted traditional broadcasting — audiences can watch what they want, when they want, on any device.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Television
cards.back: TV drama conventions: ensemble casts, multiple storylines, cliffhangers, series arcs, episodic and serial structures. Quality TV / 'peak TV' features cinematic production values.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Television
cards.back: Narrative structures: linear (chronological), non-linear (flashbacks, flash-forwards), open (unresolved), closed (resolved), single-strand, multi-strand.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Television
cards.back: Todorov's narrative theory: equilibrium → disruption → recognition → attempt to repair → new equilibrium. Many TV dramas follow this pattern within episodes and across series.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Television
cards.back: Levi-Strauss's binary opposition: narratives are structured around opposing forces — good/evil, nature/civilisation, rich/poor. Identifying these helps analyse meaning.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Television
cards.back: Barthes' narrative codes: enigma code (mysteries that drive the plot), action code (events that move the story forward), and semic code (connotations that build character).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Television
cards.back: Genre in TV: drama, comedy, documentary, news, reality TV, sci-fi, crime. Hybrids blend genres (e.g. dramedy). Genre is used to target audiences and set expectations.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Television
cards.back: Public service broadcasting (BBC, Channel 4) has a remit to inform, educate, and entertain. Commercial TV (ITV, Sky) is funded by advertising and must attract mass audiences.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Television
cards.back: Ofcom regulates UK broadcasting — it sets standards for content, protects audiences from harmful material, and ensures fair competition between broadcasters.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Television
cards.back: Watercooler moments: major TV events that generate widespread social discussion — e.g. live episodes, character deaths, or twists. Social media amplifies these shared experiences.

cards.front: What should you know about media studies exam tips — television?
cards.back: 1. For Television, use media terminology precisely (e.g. connotation, denotation, representation, ideology) 2. Always analyse how media language creates meaning for specific audiences 3. Reference specific examples from set products to support your analysis 4. When evaluating Television, consider the role of media industries and cultural contexts 5. For extended answers, debate different interpretations before reaching your own
